title: Saudi point-of-sale spending, Q2 2023 vs Q2 2022

attempts.text: In Q2 2023, the average weekly POS value increased by 10.9% compared to Q2 2022, marking a significant rise in the value of transactions across the point-of-sale (POS) system in Saudi Arabia. This increase is attributed to a rise in the average weekly transactions, which saw a 27.2% increase from 131.6 million to 167.4 million transactions. The average weekly transactions, which is a key metric for assessing the volume of sales, also increased by 27.2% year over year, indicating a robust growth in the number of transactions processed during the quarter. This growth is further supported by an average ticket, which increased by 12.8% from SAR 80.6 to SAR 90.3, reflecting a higher average spending per transaction.

attempts.text: In Q2 2023, the average weekly POS value increased by 10.9% compared to Q2 2022, marking a significant rise of SAR 1.16 billion in the value of transactions. This substantial increase is attributed to the Other category, which saw a notable rise of SAR 318 million, indicating a 20.1% increase from the previous quarter. The Restaurants & Café category also experienced a notable growth, with an increase of 27.2% in average weekly transactions, totaling 167.4 million transactions. This category's average weekly value rose to SAR 1,730 million, marking a 21.7% increase from SAR 1,421 million in Q2 2022. The Beverage and Food category also showed a notable increase, with an increase of 16.2% in average weekly value, totaling SAR 1,784 million, marking a 16.2% increase from SAR 1,535 million in Q2 2022.

final_text: Average weekly point-of-sale spending in Saudi Arabia was SAR 11.76 bn in Q2 2023, up 10.9% from SAR 10.60 bn in Q2 2022. Average weekly transactions were 167.4 million (up 27.2%), and the average ticket was SAR 70.3 (down 12.8%). The largest movements were: Other increased by SAR 318 mn; Restaurants & Café increased by SAR 309 mn; Beverage and Food increased by SAR 249 mn.
